headline: Highest risk is data leakage: gpt-researcher can read local files and use broad egress, while argo-workflows can move artifacts over APIs, creating default-path exposure and workflow misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A plausible injection path exists because gpt-researcher ingests files, citations, and MCP/API content, while argo-workflows can pass artifacts and parameters through REST/gRPC. If argo-produced content is later treated as instructions by gpt-researcher, malicious text can steer downstream behavior. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF argo-workflows outputs text artifacts that gpt-researcher parses as instructions
IF both agents share an MCP or filesystem bridge not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Add a strict content/schema validator before gpt-researcher consumes argo outputs
Prefix all inter-agent payloads with immutable provenance metadata
Disable any MCP bridge between the two agents
Use a read-only handoff directory with separate subfolders
requires-engineering: enforce instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher reads local documents and sends queries/reports through broad network egress and third-party APIs, while argo-workflows handles artifacts and parameters over APIs. If sensitive artifacts flow from argo into gpt-researcher, the pair can exfiltrate data outside the local boundary by default. The exact shared workspace is not documented, so uncertainty is resolved upward.
conditions: IF argo-workflows artifacts contain secrets or regulated data
IF gpt-researcher is allowed to read the same workspace or mounted volume
mitigations: Restrict gpt-researcher to a sanitized input directory
Remove secrets from argo artifacts before handoff
Block outbound access except approved research endpoints
Rotate any credentials present in shared files
requires-engineering: separate storage and network trust zones

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can mutate shared resources in different ways: argo-workflows writes workflow artifacts via APIs, and gpt-researcher can read files, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. If they operate on the same directory or mutable project state, concurrent writes or package changes can conflict. No locking or isolation is documented, so the overlap is material.
conditions: IF both agents target the same working directory or git checkout
IF gpt-researcher installs packages while argo-workflows is generating artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Freeze package installation during shared runs
Use file locks around mutable outputs
Run one agent at a time on shared state
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is explicitly a planner/execution/publisher stack, so it can treat upstream outputs as authoritative and then publish them. argo-workflows can supply artifacts and parameters that become inputs to that pipeline. If argo output is wrong or malicious, gpt-researcher may propagate it into reports or actions without verification, creating a strong cascade risk.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher publishes reports derived from argo-produced artifacts
IF no human or automated verification step is inserted between the agents
mitigations: Insert a verification step before publishing any derived output
Require source citations for every claim imported from argo artifacts
Mark argo outputs as untrusted in the handoff metadata
Limit gpt-researcher to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware approval gates

E_compliance.rationale: Compliance risk is driven mainly by gpt-researcher: it handles local documents, citations, and multiple third-party APIs, while argo-workflows processes artifacts and parameters. If regulated data such as EU PII or confidential documents enters gpt-researcher, retention and residency obligations may differ from argo's workflow storage. The profiles do not document matching controls, so the mismatch is plausible.
conditions: IF regulated documents or PII are placed into gpt-researcher inputs
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the same data class across both agents
mitigations: Classify inputs before handing them to gpt-researcher
Exclude regulated data from research runs
Document retention and deletion expectations for both tools
Limit secret-bearing files from shared workspaces
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
